# Warrant

> Signed records of what a repository's work is, who accepted it and who objected, that any reader re-assesses under
> its own rules. This repository keeps its own work that way, in `.warrant/`.

To ask whether you may rely on something in this repository (a release, a goal, a claim, a pull request head), you
need no clone and no configuration:

    pip install --pre "warrant-graph>=3.0.0a10"                          # rely: 3.0.0a10 and later
    warrant-agent rely github.com/s0fractal/warrant "warrant-graph==3.0.0a9"

It answers RELY, RELY ON RECORDS, WAITING, NOT DONE, SUPERSEDED or DO NOT RELY, with who accepted it and what stands
against it, read under the publisher's rules (`.warrant/v3.json`). The same command reads any repository that keeps a
`.warrant/` store, e.g. `warrant-agent rely github.com/s0fractal/minds ba1c174a`.

- [README](https://github.com/s0fractal/warrant/blob/master/README.md): what Warrant is, install, verifying a release
- [First contact for an agent](https://github.com/s0fractal/warrant/blob/master/docs/AGENT.md): reading another agent's store, and answering it from yours
- [Specification](https://github.com/s0fractal/warrant/blob/master/docs/V3.md)
- [What a store proves, and what it does not](https://github.com/s0fractal/warrant/blob/master/docs/TRUST.md)
- [Glossary](https://github.com/s0fractal/warrant/blob/master/docs/GLOSSARY.md)

Not this project: the GitHub Releases up to v0.12.0 (the retired 0.x line) and the PyPI package `warrant`.
